answers.core:
It's part of c# generators in godot.

EDIT:
Well, it seems the source generator has this:

```
string raiseMethodModifiers = signalDelegate.DelegateSymbol.ContainingType.IsSealed ?
    "private" :
    "protected";
```

Switching to this:
```
string raiseMethodModifiers = signalDelegate.DelegateSymbol.DeclaredAccessibility switch
{
    Accessibility.Protected when signalDelegate.DelegateSymbol.ContainingType.IsSealed => "private",
    Accessibility.ProtectedOrInternal when signalDelegate.DelegateSymbol.ContainingType.IsSealed => "internal",
    Accessibility.Public => "public",
    Accessibility.Internal => "internal",
    Accessibility.Protected => "protected",
    Accessibility.ProtectedOrInternal => "protected internal",
    Accessibility.Private => "private",
    _ => "protected"
};
```
Seems to build fine and works fine on my end too but then again I don't know what pitfalls are expected here, I'm not familiar with the generators much let alone godot's implementation of everything.


EDIT:
I see, the current behaviour is with MS C# guidelines in mind. But do we have to stick to the guidlines necessarily? I mean signals themselves already have automatic disconnection which is not part of guidelines, the code inside the method calls a godot EmitSignal method rather than a C# method and the EmitSignal interacts with the godot api itself.
Plus signal buses are very common patterns in games and they do need a public access in one way or another, the access decision would just be left with the user unless there are som other things I'm not aware as I mentioned above(?).
Maybe just adding an option for public ones since that's where the main difference would come from.
I'm keeping this open for a discussion anyway but thank you for pointing it out :-).
answers.workaround: The only option is to manually type out the signal emission which is the same code as in the generated methods.

title: Add an access specifier to `[Signal]` to allow the generated methods to be public
